# HFieldset

> Native grouped-control semantics and a legend.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.7.1. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HFieldset` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-fieldset>`.
- Constructor: `HearthFieldsetElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Foundation.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HFieldset.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- In Vue, disabled applies through the native fieldset to controls in the same DOM tree. For separately slotted custom elements use an owning native fieldset in the application DOM when native disabled/form association is required; a shadow-internal fieldset cannot disable controls in another root.

## Public API

label, description, disabled

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label: string;
    description?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

No component defaults; optional props are undefined (absent boolean props cast to false unless explicitly defaulted).

### Events

None

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

default

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, description, body

Use `hearth-fieldset::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HFieldset, HSwitch } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HFieldset label="Notifications" description="Choose which events you want."><HSwitch label="Deployment updates" name="deployments" /></HFieldset>
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-fieldset');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Notifications",
  "description": "Choose which events you want."
});

element.innerHTML = "<hearth-switch label=\"Deployment updates\" name=\"deployments\"></hearth-switch>"; // Static example markup only; never inject untrusted HTML.

mount.append(element);
```

## Related components

- [HInput](../input/llms.txt): A labeled input with help/error text and native validation. Web components participate in their owning form.
- [HCheckbox](../checkbox/llms.txt): A native checkbox with a mixed-state option and optional description.
- [HSurface](../surface/llms.txt): A neutral, themeable container for custom rows, toolbars, panels, and messages.
